name: git-proxy-api
description: Git Proxy API — Authelia-fronted read path to GitHub so the phone holds NO GitHub credential (#647, route 3 of #646's fallback chain). The caller authenticates to US with the Authelia bearer it already has; this service holds the GitHub token server-side and streams the result back.

native_build._cmd_doc: There are NO npm dependencies — the service is stdlib-only ESM on node:22 (http + WebCrypto for the JWKS/RS256 verify). RUN is unconditional in the image-wrapper generator, so it is spent on a syntax check of our own entrypoint: a parse error fails the BUILD instead of crash-looping a deployed container. Nothing outside this service's own source can fail its release (#254).
native_build.cmd: node --check index.mjs && node --check authz.mjs && node --check upstream.mjs && node --check contract.mjs && node --check router.mjs
native_build._apt_doc: ca-certificates only, and it is load-bearing: both outbound dependencies are HTTPS (auth.diegonmarcos.com/jwks.json for the bearer verify, api.github.com for the work). A missing trust store would not fail the build — it would 502 every request in production. No curl: the healthcheck probes with node.

deploy._compose_flags_doc: CORRECTED (#650). An earlier revision of this doc (a4107076) blamed run 36565748851's failure on the small-VM docker wrapper refusing `compose --build`. That was a FALSE ROOT CAUSE, and it is corrected here because this file had become the reference other services were copied from. Two measured facts overturn it. (1) This whole field is INERT — it never reaches the deploy host. The engine reads it once (cloud-ship-container-engine.sh: COMPOSE_FLAGS="$(get_config deploy.compose_flags)") and then only greps it to LOG A WARNING; the comment at cloud-ship-container-step-deploy-compose.sh line 121 says so outright ('`--build` in build.json's deploy.compose_flags is IGNORED'). The command actually sent is built independently at line 159 of that same script: COMPOSE_UP_FLAGS="--no-build $_PULL_POLICY $_RECREATE" — --no-build is UNCONDITIONAL, and pull/recreate derive from DOCKER_IMAGE_CHANGED/CONFIG_CHANGED, not from this string. So `--build` here could never have reached the wrapper, and no value of this field can cause or cure a deploy failure. (2) The real failure was infrastructural: the Docker daemon was DOWN on oci-analytics and would not start — 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock', rsync exit 255, 'ERROR: Docker failed to start on oci-analytics'. The engine never got as far as a compose invocation. The retry went green because the daemon came back, not because this flag changed. Most likely one memory-pressure event on a 954MB box (umami was SIGKILLed / Exited 137 with umami-setup stranded in `created` in the same window); ticketed separately. The VALUE below is kept because it is harmless and now simply agrees with what the engine does anyway — the image is built on the GHA runner and pushed to GHCR, so it must never be rebuilt on the target. Do NOT copy this field expecting it to change deploy behaviour. The invariant that actually protects the sub-2GB VMs is guarded by cloud-infra 9_others/test/small-vm-no-compose-build.test.sh, which asserts the engine always emits --no-build and never splices this field into a command.
deploy._host_doc: oci-analytics, NOT oci-apps, for two reasons. (1) It is the public-edge VM that already terminates api.diegonmarcos.com/pub (c3-public-api), so the phone reaches /git OFF-MESH — which is the whole point of route 3 versus the `gh` fallback. (2) An oci-apps ship recreates my-ai_claude-api and kills every running agent; this service has no reason to go there.

proxy._doc: auth=two_factor is what the deriver turns into the Caddy mkProtected block: `@bearer header Authorization Bearer*` -> forward_auth 10.0.0.1:4182 /auth (infra-sec_introspect-proxy), with the interactive Authelia session as the non-bearer fallback. That is exactly the credential the phone ALREADY holds (cloud-u-android ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json auth.sign_in.providers[id=authelia], kind=authelia_bearer, scope authelia.bearer.authz) — no new OIDC client, no new grant. Only /git/health is pre-auth, via the engine-supported public_paths[] array, so #646's chain has an unauthenticated reachability probe.

resources._doc: A tarball is streamed, never buffered, so memory does not scale with repository size. 128M is headroom for node's baseline plus the JWKS cache.

runtime._doc: THE endpoint contract, declared once, here. The image-wrapper generator COPYs build.json to /app/build.json, so code/contract.mjs reads this exact block at runtime and GET /git/endpoints serves it verbatim — there is no second copy to drift from. #646's client asserts against that response instead of hardcoding paths, which is the drift #371 was (client dialling 10.0.0.4 while the service deployed to 10.0.0.6).

endpoints.description: Liveness. The only pre-auth route. Returns {"status":"ok","service":"git-proxy-api"} and nothing about GitHub — an unreachable service must look unreachable, never like a 200 with an error body (#568).
This contract, verbatim from build.json runtime. Machine-readable so a client can assert its own call list against ours.

The repos the server-side GitHub credential can see. Returns {repos:[{full_name,owner,name,private,default_branch,updated_at,size_kb}]} — a projection, never the upstream body, so no upstream field can carry a credential through.

Streamed gzip tarball of :ref (query `ref`, default the repo's default branch). Proxied straight from GitHub's codeload redirect to the caller — nothing is written to disk, which is deliberate: oci disks have sat at 87-97% and an unscoped prune has destroyed services twice (#353/#393).

Recent commits of a repo in runtime.feeds.repos (query `per_page`, 1..feeds.max_per_page, default 5). Returns {repo,commits:[{sha,message,author,date,html_url}],cached_at} — a projection, not the upstream body. Undeclared repo -> 403 repo_not_declared; nothing is dialled for it. ADOPTION RULE: this route is a quota optimisation for PUBLIC data, never a dependency. The service is sheddable and the phone cannot assume it is up, so a client must treat any failure here (unreachable, 5xx, 504) as a cue to fall back to the direct public api.github.com call, and must surface that fallback's own error if it also fails — never render an empty list in place of an error.

Recent GitHub Actions workflow runs of a repo in runtime.feeds.repos (query `per_page`, same bounds). Returns {repo,runs:[{name,display_title,status,conclusion,created_at,html_url,path}],cached_at}. Read-only; there is no re-run or dispatch route. ADOPTION RULE: this route is a quota optimisation for PUBLIC data, never a dependency. The service is sheddable and the phone cannot assume it is up, so a client must treat any failure here (unreachable, 5xx, 504) as a cue to fall back to the direct public api.github.com call, and must surface that fallback's own error if it also fails — never render an empty list in place of an error.

feeds._doc: The allow-list for the commits/runs routes is DATA, here, not code: the server refuses any owner/repo not listed, so a caller cannot spend the server-side credential's quota on arbitrary repositories. Seeded from the repos the superapp Store's GitHub commits and workflow-run panels declare (cloud-u-android aa_cloud-superapp build.json ui.sections stack_observability). Every successful upstream answer is cached in memory for cache_ttl_s, keyed by (repo, kind) and always fetched at max_per_page then sliced, so the whole fleet polling costs at most 2 x len(repos) upstream calls per TTL window, however many phones ask.

upstream._token_doc: GITHUB_TOKEN arrives ONLY as a sops-decrypted env_file value (src/secrets.yaml -> dist/.secrets -> compose env_file). It is read once at startup, used ONLY in upstream.mjs#upstreamHeaders as an outbound Authorization header, and every response body this service emits is passed through redactSecrets() first. code/test-contract-and-authz.mjs mutation-proves both halves.

authelia._doc: Same three values infra-sec_introspect-proxy validates on, so a token minted for ANY existing Authelia client (cli, cloud-admin, claude-*) works here unchanged. Verified in-service as well as at the Caddy edge: the edge gate does not exist when the service is dialled directly over the mesh, and the tester has to be able to assert a refusal.

api.description: Authelia-fronted read path to GitHub: list repos, stream a tarball, and read recent commits / workflow runs of declared repos (cached, to keep the Store's feeds off the anonymous quota). The GitHub credential stays server-side; the caller only ever presents an Authelia bearer.
